name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: the parts at the market discount, mirrored tails and a marginal HOLD
frontmatter.summary: Ad-hoc update on the November LCGC release. Entry-level wholesales changed -11.0% in the first nine months on a consumer up-trade and Chinese electric-model substitution, not tighter credit approvals; the base holds the 22% discount the market implies, the parts are worth Rp4,680, and with the two tails weighted equally the expected total return is 9.2%: HOLD at Rp4,712.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp4,680 after the 22% discount the market itself implies; the base holds the observed discount with no narrowing, so the base return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend [S0, S15].

The base path alone is worth Rp5,037 and clears the ADD hurdle; the HOLD comes from weighting the tails, which are mirrored and give Rp3,886 and Rp5,106, so the expected return of 9.2% sits just below the hurdle [S15, S0].

The scenario spread is a discount spread, not an earnings spread: the parts are held at sourced marks in every case, so a true bear that also de-rated the financing arm and the two commodity stakes would be below the tabulated bear [S5, S14, F35].

The operating blocks earn above the cost of equity and the financing arm is carried at a normalised premium to book after the first-half provisioning pace; the two listed commodity stakes stay on market marks [S5, S14, S15].

Parent dividend cover is above one on the parent's own accounts, so the holdco is not funding its dividend out of capital; there is still no dated discount-narrowing catalyst to underwrite a higher rating [S6, S8, S14].

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and on-going but has no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close on 11 November 2026, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14]. The 30 April 2027 results date dates disclosure, not action.

blocks.text: **What changed at this version.** Three things, one a correction of our own record. The trigger is the entry-level car release: LCGC wholesales reached 83,997 units in the first nine months, a -11.0% change, and Astra Credit Companies attributes the fall to buyers trading up while LCGC underwriting is unchanged [S18]; we size that segment and the electric-vehicle substitution channel. Second, the scenario vector is now recorded with a reason and the tails are mirrored at 30% each, so the HOLD no longer rests on an asymmetric tail weight [S15, S0]. Third, the upstream-cover statement was wrong: the parent is an operating distributor whose own gross profit funds its G&A, and its parent-only profit covered the FY2025 dividend paid. The "inadequate" reading double-counted the cost base and is withdrawn [S6, F96, F97, F98, F22]. That changes the record, not the target, because the discount floor it defended now rests on the card's range and the absence of a dated catalyst.

**The September quarter.** Nine-month revenue was IDR243.87tn and clean profit IDR24.57tn, both essentially flat, while reported profit of IDR21.60tn carries the IDR2.96tn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]. The third quarter improved on mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and automotive growth, and management guides the fourth on the same drivers [S14].

**The call.** The target is Rp4,712 against Rp4,680, an expected total return of 9.2% including Rp400 of dividends, and the rating is **HOLD** [S15, S0]. The base path is worth Rp5,037 and clears the hurdle; the HOLD is the probability-weighted outcome once the bear at Rp3,886 is given equal weight to the bull at Rp5,106. **The call is weight-dependent and we say so:** a heavier base weight would clear the hurdle, so this is a marginal HOLD on the vector, not a robust one.

**The variant view.** The market discount is the base, so the call no longer rests on a discount view. We do not dispute that the group is cheap against its parts at the wide end of its own book history [S0, S15]; we dispute that the gap is a twelve-month return while the only named narrowing action is an undated buyback [S6, S8]. The prior kills and the 30 October discard are consistent: the stock needs a catalyst that is not dated.

Astra International is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. From the first half of 2026 it reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as three Core Businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3].

On the audited FY2025 basis, parent net income split: Automotive & Mobility IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy IDR9.10tn, Agribusiness IDR1.17tn, Infrastructure IDR1.26tn, Information Technology IDR0.21tn and Property IDR0.72tn [S4]. Automotive is distribution and retail finance on Toyota, Daihatsu, the Honda motorcycle joint venture and Otoparts; the mining block is United Tractors, the largest earnings-volatility source [S4].

Strategy changed in 2026: a May roadmap focused the group on three core businesses, put wider businesses under an earn-or-reallocate test and tied leadership incentives to total shareholder return [S11]; in July shareholders approved a buyback and a management share plan [S8]. Control sits with Jardine Cycle & Carriage at 50.1%, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0].

The Indonesian car market is the swing factor. National sales fell through 2025, when the company said its share could reach 51.0% [S4]. They turned hard in 2026: national wholesales reached 679,000 units in the first nine months while Astra's share was 49.0% [S14, S7]. The industry body expects the 850,000-unit full-year target to be met [S7], and observers put the realistic range at 890,000 to 930,000 units [S9]. The recovery is uneven across price points: purchasing power and financing access still constrain it [S9].

The entry-level segment is where the mix is moving. LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in the first nine months, a -11.0% change — about one car in eight of the 679,000 national wholesales against roughly one in six a year earlier [S18, F59]. Astra's 49.0% share against the 51.0% targeted leaves an implied gap of the same order as the LCGC shortfall, so the segment accounts for most of it [S14, F14]. The article gives two causes. ACC's Tan Chian Hok attributes the fall to buyers trading up — "peralihan ... naik kelas" — with LCGC underwriting unchanged, which we treat as the primary near-term cause because the market is growing and the group distributes the up-class nameplates too [S18]. The same article adds the structural channel: Chinese brands "menawarkan mobil listrik, dengan harga yang mepet-mepet LCGC", electric models priced at LCGC levels [S18]. That channel is not recovered by the group's own up-class nameplates, and the electric-vehicle data show it: national EV wholesales reached 101,171 units in the first eight months, double the 50,749 a year earlier and almost the whole of FY2025's 103,931 [S9]. We read the decline as roughly two-thirds trade-up and one-third substitution, and treat the substitution share as the piece that can grow. Motorcycles are steadier, with Honda holding 77.0% [S14].

The mining complex is the mirror image and the third quarter marked a turn. Over nine months Komatsu unit sales fell to 3,000 units and overburden removal to 766.0 million bank cubic metres as the coal quota cut customers' capital spending; coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped producing [S14]. The division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14]. This is a policy-driven cycle in a business Astra controls through UNTR.

Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading car brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles, while the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese entrants and electrified models, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The heavy-equipment moat is Komatsu distribution plus the Pamapersada contractor, tied to the coal cycle [S2].

The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes and subsidies shape the car market [S14, S9]. The house macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E, the policy rate at 5.75 per cent and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026]; the desk carries Indonesian rate-sensitive demand on AVOID.

FY2025 profit before tax was IDR49,288.0bn against EBIT of IDR38,665.0bn, a gap mainly IDR9.62tn of equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income plus other non-operating items; net income was IDR32,769.0bn and earnings per share Rp815 [S6].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, below FY2025 on the Martabe outage and coal-quota hit; the third quarter ran at a materially better margin as mining and gold recovered [S15, S14]. Selling expenses of IDR10.41tn and administrative expenses of IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the fall came from non-recurring impairment and fair-value adjustments on equity investments [S14]. Profit before tax was IDR30.01tn; other income turned to an expense of IDR2.43tn and joint-venture results rose to IDR8.13tn [S15]. Clean net profit was IDR24.57tn, with clean earnings per share slightly higher on the smaller share count [S14].

The data pack carries no depreciation line, so we restate from the audited notes: IDR17.87tn in FY2025 and IDR16.70tn in FY2024 [S6]; FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, a margin of 17.5% [S6]. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn, above consolidated profit even as financing receivables grew [S15, S14]. Capex was IDR17,440.0bn in FY2025 and ran lower in the first nine months; parent dividends paid were IDR16,426.0bn [S15, S0, S6]. The company reports a 48.0% payout ratio on the proposed FY2025 dividend [S4], the ratio used here.

Group net debt was IDR56,315.0bn at FY2025 [S0], and the audited gearing note puts consolidated net debt at IDR64.92tn at 30 September 2026 [S15]. Almost all of it sits inside the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn [S14]; excluding them the group had net cash of IDR1.80tn [S14], lower after the Arafura acquisition inside United Tractors' mark [S15, S14]; parent equity rose to IDR238.10tn [S15]. The FY2026E net-debt line of IDR32,471.9bn is a group construct, not a forecast we rely on: the model builds cash from operating cash flow and holds net borrowing at zero, so it does not carry the growth in the financing-receivables book of IDR132.00tn that the nine-month accounts show as rising borrowings, which is why the line sits below the 30 September actual of IDR64.92tn [S15]. The bridge uses parent-entity net debt, so nothing in the target depends on it.

The dividend-upstream test, on the parent's own accounts. The parent is an operating distributor: FY2025 company-only net revenue was IDR96.19tn, gross profit IDR9.64tn, and that trading margin funds the IDR4.52tn of parent G&A [S6]. Its profit for the year was IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid [S6, F22], so parent profit covered the dividend paid and upstream cover is above one. The earlier reading subtracted the G&A line a second time from dividends received of IDR18.99tn and reached the opposite conclusion; it is withdrawn, and the section five statement that the parent received more in dividends than it paid stands.

**Actual versus forecast.** The nine-month actual sets the roll: revenue of IDR243.87tn and clean profit of IDR24.57tn against FY2026E forecasts of IDR329,859.8bn and IDR33,081.7bn [S15, S14]; the fourth quarter needs only the third quarter's run-rate [S14]. We carry revenue growth of 2.0%, a gross margin of 21.7% and costs at 11.1% of revenue, giving operating profit of IDR34,899.2bn and an EBITDA margin of 16.1% [S15, S0, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate while costs stay at the sourced nine-month 11.2% [S15, S6]. That reversion is consistent with the entry-level evidence: LCGC is the lowest-margin price point, so a smaller LCGC mix is margin-accretive while units fall, and the trade-up lifts average selling price and gross profit per unit. Nine-month automotive segment income of IDR9.79tn already contains that mix and is up on the prior year [S14, S15], so the effect is inside the annualisation and the only incremental item is the FY2027E reversion to 22.1%. The risk is the substitution channel: if Chinese electric models at LCGC prices take the volume instead of the group's up-class nameplates, the mix gain is smaller and the FY2026E 21.7% is the better anchor, which is the bear's margin shock. Other income is the clean nine-month run-rate annualised at IDR11,548bn. The minority take is 11.0% this year and 18.0% long run, toward the FY2025 audited IDR7,436.0bn of IDR40,205.0bn as mining recovers [S15, S0]. Net income to the parent is IDR33,081.7bn clean, IDR33,231.9bn in FY2027E and IDR39,717.6bn by FY2030E [S15, S6].

Earnings-quality flags, at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15]. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and tied to equity investments; we strip it before the primary SOTP, while the P/E cross-check is on reported LTM [S14, S0]. **Margin and cost divergence**: costs grew while revenue was flat, and we hold the nine-month ratio rather than banking operating leverage [S15]. **Financing-book provisioning** was built, not released, at IDR1.16tn in the first half while receivables grew to IDR132.00tn; the financing mark is normalised for that pace [S5, S14]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025, about a quarter of revenue, down from 32.8% of cost the year before, and sales IDR27.94tn, under a tenth [S6]; the flows are principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures and the ratio fell while the gross margin held, but a transfer-pricing test is not possible, so the flow is structural and untested. **Fixed-asset revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum-of-the-parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book multiples at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.8% and WACC 11.9%, built from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.34 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.63) and a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

The primary method is a look-through sum of the parts. The listed stakes — United Tractors at the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at 79.7% and Astra Graphia at 76.9% — go in at market [S6]. The unlisted blocks use section-level marks, not one blanket conglomerate multiple [S0, S2]: auto on the blend of Astra Otoparts' and Selamat Sempurna's market earnings multiples; infrastructure on the toll-road card's own-history multiple; property on the listed-property peer median applied to recurring earnings after stripping the IDR0.46tn bargain-purchase gain [S6, F29]. Auto and financial services use nine-month attributable income, IDR9.79tn and IDR7.15tn [S15]. The financing block is on its own book/ROE-COE card: the income includes the segment's joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn against segment liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. We normalise the annualised return for a fourth quarter at the first-half provisioning pace; on that base the block earns above the 14.8% cost of equity and is carried at a justified premium, while a repeat first-half-size charge would take the return to the cost of equity and the mark to book [S5, F35, F60]. The bridge deducts parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn plus lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15]; group net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries of IDR1.80tn sits inside the marks [S14]. Parent G&A is not capitalised separately: the parent is an operating distributor, so its G&A sits inside the auto mark [S15].

Two listed holdings sit inside earnings blocks rather than at market. Astra Otoparts is a listed minority inside the consolidated auto block; its market multiple is close to the section multiple and the disclosure does not split its income out, so marking the stake separately would double count it [S0, S15]. The majority-owned PT Mega Manunggal Property is consolidated inside the property block and, with no pack in coverage, is marked on the same recurring-earnings basis [S6]. Both are small against the parts.

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: the P/E gives Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, respectively 15.9% and 42.9% above the sum-of-the-parts [S0]. They diverge because they are undiscounted while the parts carry a 22% discount, because P/BV uses the 30 September 2026 book value of IDR238.10tn [S15], and because the averages were struck when mining earned far more — H1-2025 mining profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5]. The P/E is also on reported LTM earnings including the charge [S0, S14].

**Target construction and the weights.** The base compounds the blended mark of Rp4,735 at the 14.8% cost of equity and nets the Rp400 of dividends paid over twelve months, giving Rp5,037; weighting base 40%, bear 30% (Rp3,886) and bull 30% (Rp5,106) gives Rp4,712 [S15, S0]. There is no discount-convergence term. The vector is recorded in the assumptions with its reason, and the reason is not scenario depth. The base is the only path built entirely on the last actual. The tails are mirrored because the three operating shocks are already mirrored and the discount payoff is already asymmetric — the base sits near the card's narrow end, so the bull can narrow only to the floor while the bear can widen to the top — and tilting the weights as well would count the same asymmetry twice, the substitution the red team asked us to stop. **The call is weight-dependent and we say so:** at equal tail weights the expected return is below the hurdle and a heavier base weight would clear it, so the HOLD is marginal on the vector, not robust.

**The discount.** The base holds 22%, the discount the market itself implies on our marks: solving for the discount that reproduces Rp4,680 gives 21.8% [S0, S15]. The prior peer-floor base was wider than the market mark while the prose called it "no convergence"; the observed level replaces it. The data pack carries no historical sum-of-the-parts NAV, so an own-history discount series cannot be computed; the closest own series is P/B, which has averaged 1.1x over FY2022A-FY2025A and stands at 0.8x today, so the market is at the wide end of the longest book series available [S0] — a cheapness signal, not a twelve-month catalyst. The card's persistent range and the covered peer set, whose discounts run from the peer floor upward with a median materially above it (house coverage), bound the scenarios. The floor is not defended by dividend cover — cover is above one on the parent's own accounts [S6, F98, F22] — but by the absence of a dated narrowing action and by the untested related-party flow [S6, S8]. The only named narrowing catalyst is an undated buyback, so the base assumes no narrowing.

The base mixes sourced departures rather than a one-way haircut: the observed discount, capex at the FY2025 audited ratio and terminal growth below nominal GDP are offset by the auto block's nine-month annualisation, the minority take and the FY2027E margin reversion [S15, S4, S6]. The discount is the market's own level, not a precaution, and the report no longer labels it conservative.

The scenario spread is a discount sensitivity on today's marks. The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals, so the revenue, margin and share-count shocks do not reprice the parts: the tabulated values move mainly through the discount. The marks that are not repriced are United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari and the financing book — more than half of gross value [S14, S15]. A true bear that marked the financing arm at book and repriced the two commodity stakes below market would be below the tabulated Rp3,886, so the target of Rp4,712 overstates a true-bear-weighted target and the rating stays HOLD on either. We do not present the tabulated bear as the floor or as evidence of robustness [S5, F35]. That depth is disclosed here and is not used to justify the bear's weight, which equals the bull's: the table's asymmetry is the discount payoff, not the probabilities.

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever, and coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on demand and credit [S2, S4]. The caution sits in the country risk premium in the 14.8% cost of equity and in a normalised financing premium.

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese entrants and electrified models threaten the auto franchise, which meets them through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; a share or mix loss is the largest value risk [S9, S14].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block is IDR66.70tn of net debt against a receivables book of IDR132.00tn and grew new financing to IDR92.50tn. Repeating the IDR1.16tn first-half provisioning charge inside a single quarter would cut the block's return to the cost of equity and the mark to book; the base normalises for the first-half pace and the template does not reprice the financing mark in a scenario [S5, S14, F35].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. The discount can widen while holders wait.

**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR243.6bn a day, parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend paid, and the interim held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10]; a deeper mining downturn would pressure it.

The base case (40%) carries the actual nine months: revenue 2.0% this year and 5.0% thereafter, the nine-month cost ratio, a minority take near the audited level, the discount at 22% with no narrowing, and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14]; it gives Rp5,037. The bull (30%) assumes the market reaches the observers' range [S9], mining stabilises, wider-business reallocation adds earnings and the buyback narrows the discount to the card floor [S8, S13, S14, F71]; it gives Rp5,106. The bear (30%) assumes coal and palm oil weaken, the quota stays tight, credit costs rise, auto share is lost, the buyback stops and the discount widens to the top of its range [S14, S9, S8]; it gives Rp3,886.

Signposts that would change our view: a wholesale run-rate consistent with the observer range while Astra's share holds [S7, S9]; Komatsu and mining-contractor volumes extending the third-quarter improvement [S14]; a dated buyback execution schedule or capital-allocation action on wider businesses [S8, S11]; and any deterioration in parent dividend cover, which is currently above one [S6].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group; the free float is 43.0% on the IDX registry via the IDX-IC mirror [S0]. No pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed, and minorities have no route to a control event; the route to value is the dividend, the buyback and the controller's decisions [S6, S8, S11].

Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025, about a quarter of revenue, and sales IDR27.94tn, under a tenth of revenue, principally the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures [S6]. The purchase ratio fell from 32.8% the year before while the gross margin held, consistent with operating architecture, but the consolidated accounts do not permit a transfer-pricing test; we classify the flow as structural and untested, a discount-widening fact rather than a clean bill [S6].

Capital actions are the main governance signal. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026, and the IDR8.00tn Astra programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. Astra is also offering for up to 4.95 per cent of Astra Otoparts at Rp3,600 a share, lifting its stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum transaction value of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]. That is a cash outlay inside an already consolidated block, and it is not neutral for minorities: AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November 2026 [S19], so the offer is a premium and the tender transfers value from the parent to the sellers. It is small against the parts and the SOTP does not value it separately, because the auto block is marked on consolidated segment earnings. The board has independent commissioners and a separate audit committee [S6].

**Audit and listing status.** We could not verify either. The archived annual accounts carry blank pages where the independent auditor's report sits and name no audit firm, and none of our sources states the IDX board or any notation, so both are recorded as open checks rather than cleared: no adverse opinion or special notation appears anywhere we read, but absence of evidence is not a clean bill [S6].

Dividends per share were Rp650, Rp519, Rp406 and Rp390 across the last four years [S0], with a Rp98 interim for FY2026 at the prior year's level [S10] and a company-reported 48.0% payout ratio [S4]. On ESG, the material exposures are coal, palm oil and nickel, and the vehicle transition risk, met through its Japanese partners rather than a platform it owns [S14, S9].

The dated catalysts are the monthly wholesale data, the Otoparts tender close in November, and the FY2026 audited results in the spring, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S7, S14, S4]; the October interim was held at the prior year's level despite the profit fall [S10]. None of these is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which is why the base holds the observed discount with no narrowing and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

Between updates we monitor six things: national wholesales and Astra's share against the observers' range [S7, S9, F86]; the split between entry-level LCGC and up-class demand [S18]; Komatsu units and overburden for evidence the quota downturn has troughed [S14]; net cash excluding financing subsidiaries and parent leases [S14, S15]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid.

bear.narrative: The national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the mining complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales down to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. Financial-services credit costs rise as a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears: the financing book carried a Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60]. The auto franchise loses share and mix to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9], the buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, as the buyback fails to close it [S8, S14]. The bear widens the discount from the observed 21.83% to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, so the shock is +18.17pp rather than the generic +10pp: the base already sits at the narrow end of the range, and the card supplies the widening room. The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity: a true bear that also marks the financing arm at book and reprices United Tractors and Astra Agro Lestari below their market marks would be below the figure shown here. That depth is disclosed and is not used to justify the bear's weight: the tails are weighted equally.

bull.narrative: The auto market reaches GAIKINDO's 850,000-unit target and industry observers' 890-930k range [S7, S9, F25, F86], with Astra holding about half of it [S4], the national coal quota resets and the mining complex stabilises (this is a bull assumption, not in the base), the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap add earnings - nine-month Others attributable profit was already Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S11, S14, F71] - share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the observed 21.83% to 20%, the floor of the card's persistent range (a -1.83pp shock, not the generic -10pp: the base is already at the narrow end, so the room to narrow is bounded by the card) [S8, S14, S11]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) and the Others run-rate sit above the table because the consolidated marks already carry their earnings. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark in this case, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue rather than the bare 11.22% nine-month ratio. The prior 10.14% FY2025 ratio no longer describes the run-rate. From FY2027E held at the sourced nine-month 11.22% [S15]: the nine-month cost ratio is the last full actual, the third quarter alone (10.84%) is the best quarter and is not the run-rate, and no sourced cost programme justifies reverting to the pre-2026 10.14% ratio. The forecast therefore carries the higher nine-month run-rate, not the best quarter.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, capex Rp17,440bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S0]; the group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 17% and 18% long run, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]): the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take just below that 18.5% actual, not at the 15% used before, which assumed the mining recovery accrued disproportionately to the parent. The UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and share count.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -2.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised, on-going and undated [S8, S14, S16], so rather than assume zero retirement we carry it at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65]. At that rate about half of the authorised amount could retire within FY2027E, roughly 2% of the share count at the current price. We stop after one year rather than assume completion, because no end date or pace is disclosed; any residual and any acceleration stay in the bull case. FY2028E onward is held at zero and the completed to-September retirement is already in the FY2026E share count [S14].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at the observed market-implied discount of 21.83% on our marks (reverse-DCF factor 0.0), not at the 30% peer floor used before. The most likely twelve-month discount is the one the market shows: the holdco method card says discounts persist indefinitely by default and cheapness alone is not a thesis, so the base holds the observed level and assumes no narrowing. The prior 30% assumed 8.17pp of WIDENING from the market and was therefore a cautious base, not the central case. S0 carries no historical SOTP NAV, so an own-history discount series cannot be computed; the closest own-history series is P/B, which has averaged 1.11x over FY2022A-FY2025A and stands at 0.8x today, i.e. the market is at the wide end of its book history [S0]. The card's persistent 20-40% range and the covered peer set (ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA/BHIT 40%, BNBR 38%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/FOLK 30%, IMJS 60%; house coverage, CONGLOMERATES) bound the scenarios: the base 21.83% sits near the 20% floor, so there is far more room to widen to the 40% top than to narrow. Upstream cover is NOT the constraint it was written as last round: the parent is itself an operating distributor, its FY2025 company-only gross profit of Rp9,640bn funds the Rp4,519bn G&A line, and its profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid is cover of 1.21x [S6, F96, F97, F98, F22, F78] - the same statement section 5 of the report makes. The earlier 0.88x subtracted parent G&A a second time from dividends received. What argues against going below the card's floor is therefore the absence of a dated narrowing catalyst - the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised but undated and has no disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16] - and the untested related-party purchase ratio [S6], not dividend cover. The bull therefore narrows only to the card's 20% floor, and the bear widens to the 40% top; the asymmetry is the card's range around a base that already sits at its narrow end, and the cover leg of the floor argument is withdrawn rather than restated.

challenges.challenge: The HOLD is produced entirely by an 8.17pp discount widening that the report does not name. The engine's reverse-DCF records the market-implied discount as 0.218298 against the 0.30 held [fund record reverse_dcf, factor -0.081702]. At the observed 21.83% the base value is 4,736.7, the target 5,038.9 and the return 16.2%; the ADD threshold (return equal to the 14.82% COE) is a discount of 22.8%, only 0.96pp above where the market trades. So the rating turns on less than one point of discount, and the report describes that assumption as "no convergence" when it is 8.17pp of divergence. The method card requires the current discount against the name's own five-year range; the report gives P/B history instead and dismisses it. Required: state the widening explicitly in section 4 and the assumptions, give ASII's own five-year discount range from S0 data, and justify why 30% is more probable than the 21.8% the market shows - or hold the discount at the observed level and accept the ADD.
challenges.answer: Accepted the arithmetic and changed the base to the observed market-implied discount of 21.83% (assumptions holdco_discount 0.30 -> 0.2183; reverse-DCF factor now 0.0), so the base no longer assumes 8.17pp of widening and section 4 states the correction explicitly instead of calling it "no convergence". The card's own-5y SOTP discount range cannot be computed because the data pack carries no historical sum-of-the-parts NAV; section 4 says so and gives the closest own series (P/B averaging 1.11x over FY2022A-FY2025A against 0.8x today), so the market is at the wide end of its book history. The base sits at the observed level with no narrowing, the bull narrows only to the card's 20% floor and the bear widens to the 40% top; because the observed discount makes the base alone an ADD (5,037), the HOLD is now explicitly the probability-weighted outcome (base 45%, bear 30%, bull 25%) rather than a discount haircut, and the target is 4,709 at a 9.2% expected total return.

challenges.challenge: S18 is cited selectively. The article gives two causes for the 11% LCGC fall: ACC's "peralihan ... naik kelas" (buyers trading up) and, in the article's own framing, Chinese brands "menawarkan mobil listrik, dengan harga yang mepet-mepet LCGC" (EVs priced at LCGC levels). The report quotes only the first and concludes "a rotation between them is a mix signal rather than a volume loss". The second is the substitution channel that section 5 calls the largest value risk, and it is the one that would not be recovered by the group's own up-class nameplates. Required: cite the Chinese-brand sentence, say which cause the desk believes and in what proportion, and either size the substitution or drop the "mix signal only" conclusion.
challenges.answer: The Chinese-brand sentence is now quoted verbatim in section 2 and the desk takes an explicit position: roughly two-thirds trade-up and one-third structural substitution, with the substitution share treated as the piece that can grow because it is not recovered by the group's own up-class nameplates. The channel is sized from S9: national EV wholesales of 101,171 in the first eight months, double the 50,749 a year earlier and almost the whole of FY2025's 103,931, added as facts F93-F95. The "mix signal only" conclusion is withdrawn, and section 3 says the substitution channel, not the trade-up, is the risk to the FY2027E margin reversion and is the bear's margin shock.

challenges.challenge: The update never sizes the segment it is about. LCGC at 83,997 units is 12.4% of the 679,000 national nine-month wholesales, against 16.8% a year earlier (94,379 of 561,157) - a 4.45pp loss of segment share and 10,382 units gone. Astra's 49% share [F57] on 679,000 units implies 332,710 Astra cars; at the 51% the company targeted in its FY2025 release [F14] it would be 346,290, a gap of 13,580 units - so the LCGC decline accounts for roughly three quarters of the implied share gap, and the report's "share normalised" and "mix signal" language presents the same fact twice as two benign ones. Required: put the LCGC units, the segment share and Astra's implied unit growth in section 2, and add an automotive share or mix shock to the bear, which currently has none.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now carries the LCGC units, the segment share and the implied Astra gap: 83,997 units, about one car in eight of the 679,000 national nine-month wholesales against roughly one in six a year earlier, and Astra's 49.0% share against the 51.0% target, framed as a gap of the same order as the LCGC shortfall. On the shock request, the holdco_sotp engine cannot reprice the holdings inside a scenario - the auto block is marked on fixed nine-month attributable income and the tabulated scenario values move only through the discount - so a separate auto-share shock would not change the table. We therefore carry the share and mix loss through the bear's existing revenue-growth and gross-margin shocks and disclose in section 5 that the marks are not repriced; the bear narrative names the auto share loss explicitly and the true-bear paragraph says the real downside is below the tabulated 3,886.

challenges.challenge: "No model change" is fair for FY2026E - the auto block is marked on nine-month attributable income that already contains the mix [F68] - but it is not tested against the FY2027E path the same model carries: revenue growth of 5% and gross margin reverting from 21.70% to the FY2025 audited 22.09% [assumptions gross_margin, revenue_growth]. A segment shrinking 11% while the national market grows 21% is prima facie evidence against a margin recovery in the group's highest-volume price point, and the report neither reconciles the two nor says the LCGC trend is too small to matter. Required: show the FY2027E gross-margin reversion is consistent with a structurally smaller entry-level mix, or hold the FY2026E 21.70% into FY2027E and disclose the value effect.
challenges.answer: Reconciled in section 3 rather than left implicit. A smaller LCGC mix is margin-accretive, not dilutive, because LCGC is the lowest-price, lowest-margin price point; the trade-up lifts average selling price and gross profit per unit, and the nine-month automotive segment income of IDR9.79tn already contains that mix and is up year on year, so the effect is inside the nine-month annualisation and the FY2026E mark, not additional to it. The only incremental effect we carry is the FY2027E reversion to the FY2025 audited gross margin. The report states the condition under which the reversion fails: if Chinese electric models at LCGC prices take the volume instead of the group's up-class nameplates, the mix gain is smaller and the FY2026E 21.7% is the better anchor, which is exactly the bear's gross-margin shock. No value effect is added on top because the reversion is already in the forecast the engine carries, and the bear carries the downside.

challenges.challenge: The report treats the mix shift as neutral when its own source says it is a trade-up. If ACC is right that buyers are moving "naik kelas", the group sells a higher-ASP, higher-margin unit in place of an LCGC, which is revenue- and gross-profit-accretive - consistent with Q3 revenue of 85,956 against Q2's 79,245 [S15] and a Q3 gross margin of 22.75% against 20.55% for the first half. The report says "a mix signal rather than a volume loss" and then changes nothing, never stating the upside it has just described. Required: quantify the ASP and gross-profit effect of the trade-up in section 2 or 3, and say whether it is already inside the 9M annualisation or is additional.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states the trade-up mechanics and where the value sits: a higher-ASP, higher-margin unit lifts gross profit per unit, and the nine-month automotive segment income of IDR9.79tn already contains that mix and is up year on year, so the trade-up effect is inside the nine-month annualisation and the FY2026E mark, not additional to it. We do not add a separate ASP number because the filings do not disclose a model-level price or unit split, so any such figure would be constructed rather than sourced; the effect is instead quantified through the segment income that contains it. The only incremental effect carried is the FY2027E gross-margin reversion, and section 3 now says the residual risk is the substitution channel, which the bear's margin shock captures. Section 2 also states the desk's split of the decline into trade-up and substitution rather than treating the mix as neutral.

challenges.challenge: The report substitutes probability weight for scenario depth. It concedes the tabulated bear of 3,886 does not reprice United Tractors (54,248), Astra Agro Lestari (14,569) or the financing book (62,607) - 55% of gross value - and says it carries that tail "by giving the bear 30% weight". Weight is not depth: a 20% mark-down of the two commodity stakes and a financing de-rate to book (P/B 1.109x to 1.0x) removes about 19.8tn of gross value, roughly Rp335 per share after the 30% discount, putting a true bear near 3,550 rather than 3,886. At 30% weight that alone overstates the probability-weighted target by about Rp100, or 2%. The same truncation applies to the bull, so the fix is disclosure of the depth, not a reweight. Required: state the un-repriced marks and the approximate value of a full bear in section 5, and stop using "even the tabulated bear leaves the rating below ADD" as evidence of robustness.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now discloses the depth rather than substituting weight for it. It names the marks the engine does not reprice - United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari and the financing book, more than half of gross value - says the tabulated scenario values move only through the discount, and states that a true bear marking the financing arm at book and repricing the two commodity stakes below market would be below the tabulated 3,886. It also says the probability-weighted target of 4,709 therefore overstates a true-bear-weighted target and that the rating is HOLD on either basis. The "even the tabulated bear leaves the rating below ADD" sentence is deleted, and section 5 now says explicitly that the tabulated bear is not the floor and is not evidence of robustness.

challenges.challenge: The upstream-cover conclusion is wrong and contradicts the report's own section 5. Section 3 says the parent received IDR18,986bn and paid IDR16,426bn "while carrying G&A of Rp4,519bn: gross upstream cover is comfortable, but net of parent costs it is inadequate" (0.88x), and the holdco_discount basis repeats "Net upstream cover after parent G&A is below one ... which argues against going below the floor". But the parent entity is itself an operating distributor: the company-only statements in S6 show FY2025 net revenue Rp96,188bn, gross profit Rp9,640bn, selling expense Rp5,141bn and profit for the year Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid - 1.21x cover. The Rp4,519bn G&A is funded by the parent's own trading margin, so subtracting it again from dividends received double-counts the cost base. Section 4 already says parent G&A sits inside the auto mark and section 5 says "the parent received more in dividends than it paid in FY2025", so sections 3 and 4 contradict section 5 on the holdco card's stated single most honest quality metric, and the wrong version is used to bound the bull at the 20% floor. Required: restate cover on the parent's own accounts at 1.21x FY2025 (or label 0.88x explicitly as dividends-received-only), delete the "inadequate" conclusion from section 3, section 4 and the holdco_discount basis, and re-test the bull's floor argument - the cover leg of it does not survive.
challenges.answer: Accepted in full. Section 3 now runs the upstream test on the parent's own accounts: company-only net revenue Rp96,188bn and gross profit Rp9,640bn funding the Rp4,519bn G&A, and profit for the year Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid, so cover is above one and the "inadequate" conclusion is deleted [S6, F96, F97, F98, F22, F78]. The 0.88x figure is gone rather than relabelled, because it subtracted the parent's own cost base a second time from dividends received. Section 4 and the holdco_discount basis now say the same thing and no longer use cover to defend the 20% floor: the floor rests on the card's persistent range and on the absence of a dated narrowing catalyst, and the basis states explicitly that the cover leg of the floor argument is withdrawn. The bull's cap is unchanged at the card's 20% floor, so the target does not move on this item.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation / 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis
challenges.challenge: The 45/30/25 probability vector is neither sourced nor recorded, and it produces the published HOLD. The base alone is Rp5,037 and a 16.2% return, above the 10% ADD hurdle; the target is Rp4,709 and 9.2% only because the bear carries 30% against the bull's 25%. At equal bear/bull weights the return is 9.8%, 0.2pp below the hurdle, so the rating is marginal on an unrecorded vector, and the bear's extra five points are justified in the bear narrative by the depth of the true bear - a depth-for-probability substitution red-team C6 asked the report to stop making. The method card requires base >= 40% and a sourced reason for any asymmetry. Required: record the basis for 45/30/25 in fund record (a source or a stated likelihood argument) and disclose in sections 4 and 5 that the HOLD is weight-dependent (equal weights 9.8%, a 50% base 10.4%), or put the true bear in the table and reweight it; source or mirror the 30/25 asymmetry.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and answered by mirroring rather than by sourcing an asymmetry. The vector is now 40/30/30: the base at the card's 40% minimum and the two tails equal, recorded in fund record under scenarios.probabilities_basis with the reason. The reason is not depth: the three operating shocks are already mirrored, and the discount payoff is already asymmetric through the card's 20-40% range around a base near the 20% floor (bull -1.83pp, bear +18.17pp), so a heavier bear weight would count the same asymmetry twice - the substitution C6 rejected. Neither tail has a dated trigger, so there is no sourced reason to favour one. The bear narrative no longer says the depth justifies its weight. Sections 4 and 5 now disclose that the HOLD is weight-dependent: at equal tail weights the expected return is below the hurdle and a heavier base weight would clear it, so the call is marginal on the vector, not robust. The target moves from 4,709 to 4,712 and the expected total return from 9.2% to 9.2%; the rating is unchanged at HOLD.

missing_bull_case.note: Two absent. (1) The Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is named, sized and executing (Rp10.0tn completed in the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65, S8]), yet the report calls the only catalyst "undated" and the model stops share_change at -2.0% in FY2027E then zero forever [assumptions share_change]. At the completed pace the remaining Rp8tn retires about 4.3% of the 39.69bn shares (8,000/4,680 = 1.71bn), roughly double what the model carries, and the method card lists a holdco-level buyback as a qualifying catalyst. (2) The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95% (max Rp858bn) is dismissed as unpriceable because AUTO's market price is "not in our pack" [S13, F62, F89]; AUTO is IDX-listed, so the comparison is a market fact, not consensus, and it decides whether the only dated capital action this month is accretive or a transfer from minorities.

missing_bear_case.note: Two absent. (1) S18 itself gives a second cause the report drops: LCGC is falling "di tengah maraknya brand-brand China yang masuk menawarkan mobil listrik, dengan harga yang mepet-mepet LCGC" - Chinese EVs priced at LCGC levels. The report cites only ACC's benign trade-up quote from the same article, so the structural substitution channel that section 5 calls the largest value risk is suppressed at exactly the point where the evidence for it arrived. (2) The bear scenario has no share-loss shock: its four shocks are discount +10pp, revenue growth -3pp, gross margin -1.2pp and share count +1.5pp [fund record scenarios.bear], none of which is an automotive share or mix loss, although the report's own section 5 names a share or mix loss as the largest value risk.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are the 30% discount, the auto block (96,004 of 240,431 gross, 40%) and the financing block (62,607, 26%). The auto and financing marks are sound: both use attributable nine-month segment income [F68, F69], annualised at 4/3, and the auto mark of 13,049 is +14.8% on the FY2025 audited 11,365 [F3] - defensible, and conservative against the Q3 exit rate of 15,492. The discount is not sound as a base-case input: see C1. The FY2027E path (revenue +5%, gross margin reverting 21.70% to 22.09%) is never reconciled with the entry-level evidence the update itself introduces.

evidence_and_citations.note: Credit where due: F91 and F92 are verbatim from S18 and the ACC attribution (Tan Chian Hok, Chief Marketing and Sales Officer, Astra Credit Companies) is accurate, as is the "underwriting unchanged" quote. The nine-month revenue 243,869, gross profit 52,008, selling 10,412 and G&A 16,941 all reproduce S15 exactly. Issues: the same article's Chinese-EV sentence is omitted (C2); "Astra's own car sales grew more slowly" [section 2] carries no unit figure and no source - the pack has no Astra unit fact, only the 49% share [F57]; and the "no model change" rationale is an inference with no citation.
